title: Reverse Integer
interviewTips: Clarify 32-bit signed range: should overflow return 0 or clamp? For this problem return 0 for [-2^31, 2^31-1] violation.
Trade-off: string reversal is simplest to code but uses O(log x) extra space; arithmetic pop/push is O(1) and shows overflow awareness.
Edge-case tip: explicitly mention x=0, negative x, trailing zeros e.g. 120 -> 21, and overflow cases 1534236469 and -2147483648 before coding.

approaches.name: Approach 1: String Reversal with Range Check
approaches.intuition: Reversing decimal digits is just reversing characters. Convert absolute value to string, reverse it, restore sign, then reject if outside 32-bit range.
approaches.theory: Any integer x has d = O(log10|x|) decimal digits. String conversion yields those digits in order, reversal yields reversed number ignoring leading zeros (which int() drops automatically). Using 64-bit intermediate (Python int / long long / long) lets us detect overflow after the fact by comparing against INT_MIN = -2^31 and INT_MAX = 2^31-1. Correct because reversal is bijective on digit strings except dropped leading zeros which is desired.

timeComplexity.explanation: Number of digits d = floor(log10|x|)+1. Conversion, reversal, and parsing each scan d characters.

spaceComplexity.explanation: String of d digits plus reversed copy. No other proportional storage.

approaches.name: Approach 2: Arithmetic Pop-Push with Pre-Overflow Check
approaches.intuition: Build reversed number digit by digit: repeatedly pop last digit with %10 and push with rev = rev*10 + pop. Check overflow BEFORE rev*10 overflows.
approaches.theory: Invariant: after k steps rev holds reversal of last k digits. To avoid 32-bit overflow on rev*10+pop, guard: if rev > INT_MAX/10 then rev*10 already overflows; if rev == INT_MAX/10 then need pop <= 7 since INT_MAX=2147483647. Symmetrically for negative: rev < INT_MIN/10 or rev == INT_MIN/10 and pop < -8 since INT_MIN=-2147483648. In C++/Java x%10 preserves sign, so single loop handles negatives. In Python we use abs and single positive check. This is exact because overflow condition is linear in rev.

timeComplexity.explanation: One iteration per decimal digit, d = O(log10|x|) steps, O(1) work per step.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only rev, pop, and x variables, constant extra space.
